questions.question: Figure 3 shows y = sin theta for 0 <= theta <= 360 degrees. State the coordinates of the minimum point on the curve y = 4 sin theta for 0 <= theta <= 360 degrees.
steps: The minimum of sin theta is -1 at theta = 270 degrees.
Multiplying by 4 stretches the curve vertically, so the minimum of 4 sin theta is -4.
The minimum point is (270, -4).

questions.question: On Diagram 1 (a copy of Figure 3), sketch and label the curves (i) y = 1 + sin theta and (ii) y = tan theta, both for 0 <= theta <= 360 degrees.
questions.answer: Sketch y = 1 + sin theta (sine shifted up 1, range 0 to 2) and y = tan theta (asymptotes at 90 and 270, crosses axis at 0, 180, 360)
steps: y = 1 + sin theta is the sine curve moved up by 1: it passes through (0, 1), max 2 at 90, (180, 1), min 0 at 270, and (360, 1).
y = tan theta passes through (0, 0), (180, 0) and (360, 0), with vertical asymptotes at theta = 90 and theta = 270.
Label both curves clearly on the diagram.

questions.question: Hence find the number of solutions of tan theta = 1 + sin theta that lie in (i) 0 <= theta <= 2160 degrees, and (ii) 0 <= theta <= 1980 degrees.
steps: Over one period 0 to 360: tan theta = 1 + sin theta has one root in (0, 90) (about 62 degrees) and one in (180, 270).
There is no root in (90, 180), since tan is negative but 1 + sin is at least 1; none in (270, 360) since tan is negative there but 1 + sin is at least 0.
So there are 2 solutions per 360 degrees.
(i) 0 to 2160 is 6 periods: 6 x 2 = 12 solutions.
(ii) 0 to 1980 is 5 full periods (10 solutions) plus 1800 to 1980, which matches 0 to 180 and contains one solution: total 11.

questions.question: Figure 5 shows part of the curve C with equation y = sin(x/12), x in radians. State the period of C.
steps: The period of sin(x) is 2pi.
For sin(x/12), the period is 12 x 2pi = 24pi.

questions.question: The point M on C is a minimum point. State the coordinates of M.
steps: Minimum of sin(x/12) is -1, when x/12 = 3pi/2.
So x = 18pi and y = -1, giving M = (18pi, -1).

questions.question: The smallest positive solution of sin(x/12) = k is alpha. In terms of alpha, find (i) the negative solution of sin(x/12) = k that is closest to zero, and (ii) the smallest positive solution of cos(x/12) = k.
steps: Solutions of sin(x/12) = k are x = alpha, 12pi - alpha, and their shifts by 24pi. Here alpha < 6pi since k > 0 and alpha/12 < pi/2.
(i) Negative solutions are alpha - 24pi and -12pi - alpha. The one closest to zero is -12pi - alpha.
(ii) cos(u) = sin(u0) when u = pi/2 - u0, so cos(x/12) = k has smallest positive solution x = 12(pi/2 - alpha/12) = 6pi - alpha.

questions.question: Figure 2 shows part of y = cos 2x, x in radians. The point P is a minimum point on the curve. State the coordinates of P.
steps: Minimum of cos u is -1 at u = pi, so 2x = pi.
x = pi/2 and y = -1.

questions.question: On Diagram 1 (a copy of Figure 2), sketch the curve with equation y = sin x.
questions.answer: Sine curve through (0, 0), max 1 at pi/2, zero at pi, min -1 at 3pi/2, period 2pi
steps: y = sin x passes through the origin and rises to a maximum of 1 at x = pi/2.
It crosses the x-axis at pi and 2pi, with a minimum of -1 at x = 3pi/2.
Its period is 2pi, so it repeats with the same shape across the diagram.

questions.question: Hence, or otherwise, deduce the number of solutions of cos 2x = sin x that lie in (i) 0 <= x <= 20pi and (ii) 0 <= x <= 21pi.
steps: Use cos 2x = 1 - 2 sin^2 x, so 1 - 2 sin^2 x = sin x, giving (2 sin x - 1)(sin x + 1) = 0.
So sin x = 1/2 (x = pi/6, 5pi/6 per 2pi) or sin x = -1 (x = 3pi/2 per 2pi): 3 solutions per period 2pi.
(i) 0 to 20pi is 10 periods, giving 30 solutions (none at the endpoints).
(ii) 20pi to 21pi adds pi/6 and 5pi/6 beyond 20pi (3pi/2 is outside), giving 30 + 2 = 32.

questions.question: Figure 3 shows y = tan x and the line l with equation y = pi x, for -pi < x < pi. State the period of tan x.
steps: tan x repeats every pi radians.
So the period of tan x is pi.

questions.question: Write down the number of roots of tan x = (pi + 2)x in the interval -pi < x < pi.
steps: x = 0 is always a root, since both sides are zero.
The line has gradient about 5.14, steeper than tan's gradient 1 at 0, so on (0, pi/2) tan x - (pi+2)x goes from negative to positive: one root.
By odd symmetry there is one root in (-pi/2, 0), and none in the other branches, giving 3 roots.

questions.question: Write down the number of roots of tan x = pi x in the interval -2pi < x < 2pi.
steps: x = 0 is a root.
On (0, pi/2) there is one root, since tan x - pi x is convex and starts at 0 with negative gradient.
On (pi, 3pi/2) tan rises from 0 to infinity and meets pi x once, near x of about 4.6.
With odd symmetry this gives 1 + 2 + 2 = 5 roots.

questions.question: Write down the number of roots of tan x = pi x in the interval -100pi < x < 100pi.
steps: Each branch of tan with centre k pi (k >= 1) contains exactly one positive root, just after k pi + 0.97.
Positive branches k = 1 to 99 lie inside (0, 100pi), giving 99 roots, plus one root in (0, pi/2): 100 positive roots.
By symmetry there are 100 negative roots, and x = 0 is also a root.

questions.question: Figure 1 shows part of the curve C1 with equation y = 4 cos x degrees. P is a minimum point and Q lies on the x-axis. State (i) the coordinates of P, and (ii) the coordinates of Q.
steps: Minimum of 4 cos x is -4, when cos x = -1, which is at x = -180 in the figure.
Q is a zero where cos x = 0 after 360 degrees, at x = 450.

questions.question: C2 has equation y = 4 cos x degrees + k, where k is constant. C2 has minimum y value -1. R is the maximum point on C2 with smallest positive x coordinate. State the coordinates of R.
steps: Minimum of 4 cos x + k is -4 + k = -1, so k = 3.
Maximum value is 4 + 3 = 7, occurring when cos x = 1.
The smallest positive x with cos x = 1 is x = 360.

questions.question: Figure 4 shows y = sin x. Given sin alpha = p, where 0 < alpha < 90 degrees, state in terms of p the value of (i) 2 sin(180 - alpha), (ii) sin(alpha - 180), and (iii) 3 + sin(180 + alpha).
steps: sin(180 - alpha) = sin alpha = p, so 2 sin(180 - alpha) = 2p.
sin(alpha - 180) = -sin alpha = -p.
sin(180 + alpha) = -sin alpha = -p, so 3 + sin(180 + alpha) = 3 - p.

questions.question: On Diagram 1 (a copy of y = sin x), sketch the graph of y = sin 2x.
questions.answer: Sketch with period 180 degrees, zeros at 0, 90, 180, max 1 at 45, min -1 at 135
steps: sin 2x has period 180 degrees, half that of sin x.
It passes through the origin and reaches its maximum of 1 at x = 45 degrees.
It crosses the x-axis at 90 and 180 degrees, with minimum -1 at x = 135 degrees.

questions.question: Hence, in terms of alpha, find the x coordinates of any points in the interval 0 < x < 180 degrees where sin 2x = p.
steps: Let u = 2x, so 0 < u < 360 and sin u = p with p > 0.
Solutions in (0, 360) are u = alpha and u = 180 - alpha.
Dividing by 2 gives x = alpha/2 and x = 90 - alpha/2, both in (0, 180).

questions.question: Figure 3 shows part of y = f(x), a trigonometric function. Write down an expression for f(x).
steps: The curve has maximum 3 at x = 0 and minimum -3 at x = +/- pi.
This is the cosine curve with amplitude 3.
So f(x) = 3 cos x.

questions.question: On a separate diagram, sketch for -2pi < x < 2pi the graph of y = f(x + pi/4), showing clearly the coordinates of all points where the curve meets the axes.
questions.answer: y-intercept (0, 3/sqrt(2)); x-intercepts at x = pi/4 + n pi; max 3 at -pi/4 and 7pi/4; min -3 at 3pi/4 and -5pi/4
steps: y = 3 cos(x + pi/4) is f shifted left by pi/4.
y-intercept: x = 0 gives 3 cos(pi/4) = 3/sqrt(2), about 2.12, so (0, 2.12).
x-intercepts: x + pi/4 = pi/2 + n pi gives x = pi/4 + n pi, i.e. pi/4, -3pi/4, 5pi/4, -7pi/4.
Maxima at x = -pi/4 and 7pi/4 (value 3); minima at 3pi/4 and -5pi/4 (value -3).

questions.question: Figure 4 shows part of y = g(x), a trigonometric function, for -2pi < x < 2pi. Write down an expression for g(x).
steps: The curve crosses the axis at the origin, rising, with maximum 1 at x = pi/4 and minimum -1 at x = -pi/4.
Period is pi, so the function is sin 2x (period 2pi/2 = pi).
So g(x) = sin 2x.

questions.question: On a separate diagram, sketch for -2pi < x < 2pi the graph of y = g(x) - 2, showing clearly the y-intercept.
steps: Shift the graph of sin 2x down by 2.
The maxima become -1, minima become -3, and the period stays pi.
At x = 0, y = sin 0 - 2 = -2, so the y-intercept is (0, -2).

questions.question: Figure 2 shows y = f(x) where f(x) = cos 2x degrees for 0 <= x <= k. Point Q is a minimum point and R(k, 0) lies on the curve. State (i) the coordinates of Q, and (ii) the value of k.
steps: Minimum of cos 2x is -1, when 2x = 180, so x = 90: Q = (90, -1).
After Q the curve rises to a maximum at x = 180, then falls to zero at 2x = 450.
So R is the zero at x = 225, giving k = 225.

questions.question: For f(x) = cos 2x degrees, 0 <= x <= k (k = 225 from part (a)): given that there are exactly two solutions to the equation cos 2x degrees = p in the region 0 <= x <= k, find the range of possible values for p.
steps: With k = 225, let u = 2x degrees so 0 <= u <= 450 and cos u = p.
For 0 < p < 1 there are 3 solutions (two in (0, 360) and one in (360, 450)); p = 0 gives 3 as well.
For -1 < p < 0 there are exactly 2 solutions in (90, 270).
p = 1 gives u = 0 and u = 360, exactly 2 solutions; p = -1 gives only 1.

questions.question: Figure 3 shows part of the curve C1 with equation y = 3 sin x degrees. P is the first maximum point and Q is a zero to the right. State (i) the coordinates of P, and (ii) the coordinates of Q.
steps: The first maximum of 3 sin x is at x = 90, so P = (90, 3).
Zeros of 3 sin x are at multiples of 180; the figure shows Q after a maximum at 450 and a minimum at 270.
The zero at 540 gives Q = (540, 0).

questions.question: C2 has equation y = 3 sin x + k with maximum y value 10. R is the minimum point on C2 with smallest positive x coordinate. State the coordinates of R.
steps: Maximum of 3 sin x + k is 3 + k = 10, so k = 7.
Minimum of 3 sin x + 7 is -3 + 7 = 4, when sin x = -1.
The smallest positive x with sin x = -1 is 270, so R = (270, 4).

questions.question: Figure 4 shows part of y = A cos(x - 30) degrees, where A is constant. P(30, -3) is a minimum point. Write down the value of A.
steps: At x = 30, cos(x - 30) = 1, so y = A.
P is a minimum with y = -3, so A = -3.
(A = 3 would make (30, 3) a maximum, which contradicts the figure.)

questions.question: Q is a maximum point of the curve in Figure 4. Find the coordinates of Q.
steps: y = -3 cos(x - 30) has maxima where cos(x - 30) = -1, i.e. x = 210 + 360n.
The maxima are at 210, 570, 930, ...; Q is the third maximum to the right of P, as drawn in Figure 4.
Maximum value is -3 x (-1) = 3.

questions.question: Figure 4 shows part of C1 with equation y = 3 cos(x/n) degrees, x >= 0. C1 cuts the positive x-axis first at P(270, 0). State (i) the value of n, and (ii) the period of C1.
steps: The first zero of cos(x/n) is at x/n = 90, so 270 = 90n, giving n = 3.
Period of cos(x/n) is 360n = 360 x 3 = 1080 degrees.
So n = 3 and the period is 1080 degrees.

questions.question: Point Q is a minimum point of C1 (y = 3 cos(x/3) degrees). State the coordinates of Q.
steps: Minimum of cos(x/3) is -1 when x/3 = 180.

questions.question: C2 has equation y = 2 sin x degrees + k. Points R(a, 12/5) and S(-a, -3/5) lie on C2, with a a constant less than 90. Find the value of k.
steps: Sine is odd: sin(-a) = -sin a.
Adding the equations: 2 sin a + k = 12/5 and -2 sin a + k = -3/5 gives 2k = 9/5.
Check: 2 sin a = 3/2, so sin a = 0.75 and a = 48.6 degrees, which is less than 90.
